result:
The proposed answer of {2, 3, 5} is not supported. The solution cites no actual theorem for the Γ₀-type subgroups. It conflates this problem with the results on principal congruence subgroups Γₙ(p), which are a different family.

My recollection of the relevant result for n = 3 is that H³(Γ₀,₃⁺(p); ℚ) vanishes exactly for p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 13}. These are the primes for which X₀(p) has genus zero, apart from p = 11, which is not in the set. The sum would then be 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 13 = 30, not 10. I am recalling this from memory and have not verified it against the paper. It is still enough to show the proposed set is too small, since p = 7 and p = 13 would also belong to it.

VERDICT: REJECT
